Messages.Author: KevinM
Messages.Body:
Pentex Subversion is an auto-include in EVERY DECK and players are forced to design their decks, every deck, with this card in mind. It's stupidly, ridiculously powerful, and while I have no objection to the card effect itself, I think it should never have been printed in that form.

Either a Once Per Game or Once Per Methuselah restriction would be absolutely fine with me, as I've studied the card and I don't see a blood or pool cost that would be fair to the player.

Messages.Author: Dorrinal
Messages.Body:
Not while No Secrets From The Magaji exists.

Edit: I believe the game would be better without such strong counters to tapping tech. The only other answer to something like NSFTM is block-fails, and I like that interaction, but I don't like the way NSFTM is a hard counter to tap-and-bleed.

Messages.Author: Haze
Messages.Body:
It's definitely undercosted for both offense and defense. Though I'm not saying bumping the price up to 3 or 4 pool would make it better. It should've been one effect or the other, but not both at once.

and once-per-methuselah doesn't convince me. I've seen too many games where it was played only once but stuck around until the end (usually contesting)

If it were 2 pool just to prevent blocking only, then maybe it'd be a balanced card. what does everyone think about this? Nothing wrong with ousting faster and lunging, when it works right.

The effect about no acting is what slows down the game, and means everyone needs to pack several copies so they can contest. It becomes too versatile; play it on your prey and even if you don't oust them you still prevent them from going forward at full speed. Or, play it on your predator's first vampire and enjoy a few relaxed turns of no pressure at all. If it's stuck on you, the best way to get rid of it is usually to contest it the whole game.

another idea is if the card were easier to remove. maybe you pay some pool, or how about it automatically burns on the player's next untap?

Messages.Author: Xaddam
Messages.Body:
Without Pentex gaining VPs would be harder. It's already hard as it is, removing (or decreasing the power of) pentex would make dominate a better strategy and non-dominate a worse strategy. It's a shame that's it's an auto-include, since it makes deck-building dull. But the card is good for the game.

Just stop trying to make a 10-cap block deck work. It would be a useless high risk-low yield strategy even without pentex in the game.

Adam Esbjörnsson,
Prince of Örebro

Messages.Author: AaronC
Messages.Body:
I agree that there is a place for Pentex-like card in the game, but as written it is just too powerful. The last two times I got it played on me was by a wallish prey. It can easily take three actions just to get the damned thing off when you have so much better to do. If it can't be changed (since errats would apparently end the world as we know it), it should be banned.

I can think of two games in which it saved the ass of my super-star because I got to contest it. Did I really want to put Pentex in those decks? No - but I couldn't afford to lose my star minion. Pentex just gets so old, so fast.

Above all, the minion who is the target of Pentex should at least be able to attempt to remove it as their sole available action.

Messages.Author: Bell
Messages.Body: Pentex is fine as it is, played at the correct time/situation it *can* be a devastating card - so can many others. It is a gross exaggeration to say that it's an auto-include or that every deck needs to be designed with this card in mind. Many decks I design ignore it altogether - just as I might choose to ignore combat or vote defense - when you do so, it is at your own peril but not because the card is overly powerful, but because it is good. Ignoring anything has risk involved, there are many decks which can ignore this card or will be unaffected by it unless played at an ideal time.

Messages.Author: Pagan
Messages.Body:
> Giving +1 stealth to remove it won't change anything. Wall deck will still defend it, aggressive decks will still oust you the turn its played.
>
So a wall deck protecting one of its resources is a bad thing for the game?

If an agressive deck ousts you because one minion is locked up then you took that risk when you made the deck, and likely won other games because your one minion blocked every action in the game even remotely threatening.(I'm looking at you Cesewayo.)

And giving the action +1 stealth would make a significant number of removal attempts succeed that don't because of Jake or other random, non +intercepting, minions block. It doesn't change the initial impact but not every play of a Pentex results in an oust or everyone would play 15 of them.

Instead of changing Pentex what if a new master was added.

I Hate Pentex
Type: Master
Cost: 2 pool
Master: trifle.
Burn a card you control or one played on a minion you control. A Methuselah may only play one I Hate Pentex each game.

Sudden stops an ousting turn lunge and this would stop a scenario where your game is locked up because your one minion is stuck and you didn't have a Sudden in hand when it was played. It also has other uses and likely needs to be once/game to stop some Bauble/Serpentis shennanigans from happening much easier than they already do.

Removing Pentex from the game is nothing but bad for it as we should remove all cards that result in players being ousted then and spend 2 hours discarding Eyes of the Dead every turn as we all get .5VPs.

Messages.Author: Haze
Messages.Body:
enough with the retarded ad hominem arguments about deck building skills, go over  to this forum if you want that.

the point about bigcaps/superstars is a valid one. if your vampires are expensive, then you get harmed by Pentex a lot more than a midcap deck, and a weenie deck really doesn't care about losing 1 minion. this means that bigcap decks are weaker than weenie decks, especially due to how often Pentex appears in tournaments! (hint: it's very very common)

you have to back away from the issue, this isn't a matter of "how do I win a tournament" but "how do we balance VTES"

I still believe that the "no acting" clause of Pentex is the real problem, while shutting down a blocker is fine. losing a strong blocker sucks, but the same result is possible by Seduction or Block Fails, so it's still fair. On the other hand, losing a good portion of your acting power on your own turn completely ruins the game for bigcap decks, and they have fewer actions to begin with! from what's pretty much an unblockable Sensory Deprivation. and then they get fewer actions to attempt to remove Pentex as well. it's completely stacked against them, yet barely even irritates a weenie deck. the weenie decks still have a huge advantage here.

Minion Tap needed to be un-nerfed to allow players to even build bigcap decks. now Pentex needs to be nerfed to give them a competitive chance.

Around here Pentex is rarely burned cross-table because people don't have those kinds of actions to spare, or the vampire that's Pentexed is so scary they prefer the situation as is. Believe me when my assault-gun wielding Assamite got Pentexed twice in a game, no one offered to remove Pentex.

The minion who's Pentexed should at least have the right to try to remove it himself, so the Methuselah who played it has to deal with that vampire's stealth or combat. If a Big Brother corporation has closed my accounts, shut down my phone, and placed goons outside my haven, I should have a chance to get out myself, either by sneaking or fighting the goons. I imagine removing Pentex to be similar to the plot of the Sandra Bullock movie The Net.

From a source material perspective, I can see how the Pentex Corporation could paralyze the minion so much he can neither continue with his normal activities nor help protect his master, but I don't see how it could completely take away his ability to act.

> I can understand that it sucks the proverbial balls when your first vamp gets slapped with one and nobody on the table will assist in the removal, but the player who afflicted you with such a curse still needs to keep one of his own minions up for block attempts, 2 pool is nothing to sneer at and it is my belief that high cap decks have had more then enough love to bring them up to par with others (e.g. Villein).
>
> I have seen a players 11 cap get the van outside the house without ever taking an action, yet he still went on to win the final. The 'poor me' stance, I am now useless and to be ignored can be an effective tool if you believe your still in it and your game isn't ruined.
>
Aaron
Archbishop
Adelaide
